questions.q: What do Report Builder and SSDT's Report Designer both ultimately produce?
options: The same kind of file — an RDL report definition
Completely different, incompatible report formats
Report Builder produces RDL; SSDT produces a different XML format
Neither produces a saved file until published to Power BI
questions.explain: Both tools are front doors onto the same underlying RDL format — neither is 'the real one.' The difference is the working style around authoring, not the file format.

options: A stand-alone, Office-like authoring app that doesn't require a project or Visual Studio
A command-line-only tool for report deployment
A feature inside SQL Server Management Studio
A wizard that only runs inside SSDT
questions.explain: Report Builder is stand-alone — you can launch it directly from the web portal's New menu, with no Visual Studio or project involved.

questions.q: What does SSDT's Report Server Project structure give you that Report Builder doesn't?
options: Source control integration and a Configuration Manager for switching between deployment property sets
The ability to publish directly to the Power BI service
An Office-like ribbon interface
The ability to preview a report without any data source
questions.explain: SSDT's project-based structure adds source control integration and Configuration Manager, letting you switch between named configurations like Debug (test server) and Release (production).

questions.q: What's a real limitation of Report Builder mentioned in this lesson?
options: You can't create a new shared data source from scratch — only browse to and select an existing one
It cannot deploy reports to a report server at all
It requires Visual Studio to be installed
It cannot open reports created in Report Designer
questions.explain: In Report Builder you can browse to and select an existing shared data source, but you can't create one from scratch — that requires SSDT's Report Designer.

questions.q: Which tool can publish a paginated report directly to the Power BI service?
options: Report Builder
SSDT's Report Designer only
Neither tool supports this
Only the web portal, never an authoring tool
questions.explain: Report Builder can deploy to a native-mode or SharePoint-integrated report server, or publish straight to the Power BI service.
